headline: China's silent war for Taiwan has long begun
lead: Beijing is trying by all means to destabilize Taiwan without a single shot being fired. Sinologist and intelligence expert Jürgen Kremb describes in the podcast «NZZ Geopolitik» how China is undermining the island with cyberattacks, disinformation, and espionage.
seo_title: China's strategy: Hybrid war against Taiwan without armed force
social_title: Taiwan in the crosshairs: China's gradual approach without military force
print_subtitle: Beijing is attempting to destabilize Taiwan through cyberattacks and disinformation.
summary_bullets_en: China is waging a hybrid war against Taiwan to destabilize the island and force unification, using methods such as cyberattacks, disinformation, and espionage.
Xi Jinping views control over Taiwan as a personal mission and sees it as a threat to the Communist Party's legitimacy.
The West is warned not to remain idle, as similar threats could affect other democratic societies.

original_de.headline: Chinas stiller Krieg um Taiwan hat längst begonnen
original_de.lead: Peking versucht mit allen Mitteln, Taiwan zu destabilisieren, ohne dass auch nur ein Schuss fällt. Der Sinologe und Geheimdienstexperte Jürgen Kremb schildert im Podcast «NZZ Geopolitik», wie China die Insel mit Cyberangriffen, Desinformation und Spionage unterwandert.

body.text: _Your opinion matters: How do you like the podcast «NZZ Geopolitik»? _

«Beijing is waging a hybrid war to wear down the democratic island republic and force a unification,» says veteran China correspondent Jürgen Kremb. In the new episode of «NZZ Geopolitik,» the sinologist recounts the methods of this war: from millions of daily cyberattacks on critical infrastructure such as water and electricity works, to the targeted flooding of social networks with fake news by troll armies.

The Chinese’s goal, Kremb says, is to divide society in Taiwan and break its will to resist. Kremb, who himself was pursued in Taiwan by a suspected agent, says the West must not stand by idly: «What is happening in Taiwan also threatens us as free and democratic societies. We must wake up.»

For China’s President Xi Jinping, Kremb says, the annexation of Taiwan is, on the one hand, a personal mission to secure his place in history. On the other hand, he adds, the mere existence of a free and democratic Taiwan is considered a fundamental threat to the legitimacy of the Communist Party.
_All episodes of «NZZ Geopolitik: Understanding the Big Picture» can be found in this overview._
